paragraphs: Rabbi Shmuel, son of Rabbi Simon.
In Ruth Rabbah 3:6, he says, “That day was the omer harvest.” Hyman notes that Yalkut Ruth, remez 601, names R’ Shmuel bar Nachmani instead.

notes.text: The supplied Ruth Rabbah locator פ״כו remains unresolved; historical OCR has a possible 3:6 form. The Yalkut numeral תרא is 601.

The saved whole Torat Emet Ruth Rabbah3:6 scalar explicitly names Rabbi Shmuel son of Rabbi Simon and the omer harvest. Earlier negative results for קציר העומר missed the defective העמר spelling and are withdrawn as absence support. The match is retained alongside literal פ״כו; no printed-numeral or transcription-history verdict follows. Yalkut רמו תרא is conventionally remez601 by numeral arithmetic; its abbreviated Shmuel bar Nachmani variant remains Hyman’s uninspected report, not a full-title or identity harmonization.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 1146) gives Ruth Rabbah פ״ג־ו and Yalkut רמז תרא, where the supplied transcription has פ״כו and רמו. The consulted Ruth Rabbah 3:6 names Shmuel son of Rabbi Simon. The corresponding passage in Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 601 names Shmuel bar Nachmani for the omer harvest and cites him again in a separate teaching about the barley harvest.
